ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy d94bc37 by mike.leblanc, applied to production switches at 02:11Z via automated deploy e02f118, disabled IGMP snooping on VLANs 100-300 across all core switches as part of a multicast rollout preparation. Without IGMP snooping, switches could not constrain multicast traffic to registered ports and instead flooded it to all ports on each VLAN. This triggered a layer-2 broadcast storm that saturated switch CPUs, caused CAM table overflows, and induced a spanning tree topology change storm. The resulting network partition made all datacenter services including frontend, cart-service, checkout-service, postgres, redis, kafka completely unreachable, causing a global outage with 98.7% error rate.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately re-enable IGMP snooping on all affected VLANs via out-of-band switch management (emergency CLI access to core switches). 2. Revert igmp_settings.yaml from commit d94bc37 to restore snooping-enabled configuration and re-push to all switches. 3. Allow STP to reconverge and validate multicast flood has subsided (traffic below 200 Mbps threshold). 4. Confirm all service health checks pass before declaring all-clear. 5. Post-incident: require a staged rollout with canary switch testing and a network traffic impact assessment before any IGMP configuration changes are applied datacenter-wide.
